data.name: The Queer Jam
data.description:
Sundays just got a little gayer! 'The Queer Jam is a new monthly improv show and jam celebrating the LGBTQ+ and queer community, taking over the Sunday Jam, every second Sunday at 5p.

The evening begins with a set from a rotating cast of queer performers, followed by an open jam for (queer only!) improvisers of all levels. Come play, meet people, try stuff, and make some weird little comedy together. Allies are welcome to watch and support from the audience.

Can't make it this time? Catch us every month -- second Sundays (replacing the Jam). Anyone planning on jamming can reserve a ticket for free!

------------------------------------------------------------

FAQs

1. What does “queer-only” mean?
It means the performers on stage is only for people who identify as queer. If that’s you and you want to be in the jam, come!

2. Can straights come to the show?
Yes! We welcome all audience members. Just know that the stage belongs to the queer community. Sit back, laugh, and support some dope comedy.

3. Can I perform in a future show?
If you identify as queer and you’re interested in bringing the funny, come by and put your name in the bucket for the jam portion! That's stage time for you! If you're interested in other ways to perform, let’s talk! Each month will feature an improv set from experienced improvisers in the area, plus sometimes even a stand-up or storyteller!

4. Should I get tickets in advance?
YES. The show may sell out and that's the only way to guarantee space.

5. Is the venue accessible?
Our venue is accessible! There are no stairs, and the first couple of rows are on the floor with movable chairs. The bathroom (yes, singular) is on the same level and accessible to anyone who needs it.

6. Will there be content warnings?
It’s improv comedy—so there's no script. We try to keep things safe and fun for everyone in the room, however because it is all made up on the spot you can expect some adult language and themes, or at least a high probability. If any show includes anything that might need a more specific heads-up (e.g., sensitive topics or flashing light show), we’ll post about it in advance.

Did we forget something? If there's something we didn't address that you still have questions on, please don't hesitate to reach out!

No passes, coupons, or Groupon vouchers will be accepted for this performance.

About Chris:

Chris Higgins is a nationally touring comedian from Colorado, now based in Chicago, who brings a unique blend of stoner wisdom, masterful impressions, and outdoorsy sensibilities to stages across the country. Known for his viral stand-up clips that have amassed millions of views, his online sketch series "God n Angel" (1.6M followers), and his comedy special "Live at the Fort," Chris is quickly establishing himself as one of comedy's most distinctive rising voices.

A festival favorite, Chris has performed at the New York Comedy Festival, Netflix is a Joke Comedy Festival, and High Plains Comedy Festival, while taking home "Best of the Fest" honors at both Westend Comedy Festival and 10,000 Laughs Comedy Festival. His comedy has been featured on Don't Tell Comedy, ViceTV, Bob & Tom, and he's currently selling out stops nationwide.

Chris's comedy attracts fans of comics like Rory Scovel, Kyle Kinane, and Mitch Hedberg - audiences who appreciate clever wordplay, unexpected perspectives, and a comedian who proves you can be both laid-back and razor-sharp. Chris combines Colorado's outdoor spirit with Chicago's comedy hustle to create something entirely his own.

data.description: Buying a ticket means you consent to potentially being on camera. ARRIVAL INFO:Please arrive early to be seated and experience any of the pre-built pre-show. We recommend showing up at least 30 minutes before show time. Once the show begins there is no late seating because the cameras will be rolling. Wait, What’s Sri Lanka? is a one hour stand-up special, written by Shenuque and directed by Sunny Laprade, this show is for anyone who has ever felt invisible. The show explores the joy of embracing all parts of your identity while navigating the pain of not feeling seen. Shenuque uses a narrative stand-up style to talk about their life through the lens of being Sri Lankan and how that intersects with their other identities. The show reveals how interconnected we all are. Regardless of whether or not you're Sri Lankan, this show is for you. Topics include race, gender, sexuality, and of course, aunties. If you enjoy stand-up comedy that weaves together humor with a compelling narrative, you will enjoy this show.All graphics are designed by: Elliot Davis.Music by: DJ UshkaOriginal Music by: Roshane KarunaratneBio:Shenuque is a Sri Lankan American comedian born and raised on Staten Island. Their stand-up is infused with a passion for storytelling and an enrapturing stage presence. They are currently touring their debut stand-up special, Wait, What’s Sri Lanka?, a show for anyone who has ever felt invisible. They’ve graced the stage in Off-Broadway productions and contributed their writing talents to HBO Max. They’ve worked as a director for the Murmuration Theater Company and co-founded the award-winning podcast studio Many Sided Media, where you can regularly hear their voice acting on the show My First Dungeon. Audiences have said that Shenuque is like if Hasan Minhaj, Tiffany Haddish, and John Mulaney were in a polycule and didn’t let Shenuque in, so he modeled his comedy after all of them.

data.description: Tim Dillon is a stand-up comedian, writer, and actor known for his no-holds-barred humor and incisive social commentary. On April 15th, Dillon released his highly anticipated stand-up special, I’m Your Mother on Netflix worldwide. Filmed at The Mothership in Austin, the special is a no-holds-barred, unapologetic ride through today’s chaos. With his signature humor, Dillon tackles everything from his odd loyalty to the British royal family to roasting the world’s absurdities and more with no filter. Last fall, the comedian released his Netflix special, Tim Dillon: This Is Your Country, which took on the political and cultural chaos leading up to the 2024 election. Framed as a Jerry Springer-style talk show, the special explores controversial topics and human behavior through Dillon’s interactions with real people and his trademark boldness. Dillon first made waves with his 2022 Netflix special, Tim Dillon: A Real Hero, in which he rants about fast food, living in Texas, Disney adults, and the reason no one should be called a hero. He originally appeared on Netflix in 2018 with a short set as part of The Comedy Lineup. Dillon’s podcast, The Tim Dillon Show, averages a million viewers a week between video and audio downloads. He tours theaters internationally and has been a guest on The Joe Rogan Experience 15 times. On-screen, Dillon recently starred in Eli Roth’s box office hit Thanksgiving and appeared in Todd Phillips' Joker: Folie à Deux.
